violation_type.title: AP Parental Communication - Sign or Symptoms Requiring Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.307(b)(2))
violation_type.short_title: AP Parental Communication - Sign or Symptoms Requiring Hospitalization
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, it was determined that both parents were not contacted during a medical emergency.

finding_variants.text: Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, it was determined that both parents were not contacted during a medical emergency.

Based on the observations made during the DFPS investigation, a parent of a child who suffered a medical emergency while in care was not accurately notified of the details of the child?s medical emergency.

During the course of the investigation, it was verified that parents of a child who displayed symptoms of a seizure were not immediately notified of the event, but were notified hours later at their regular pick up time, resulting in a delay in the child receiving medical evaluation and treatment.

During this investigation, the operation failed to notify a child's parent that their child was demonstrating signs of having a possible seizure while in care. The child's symptoms are to include fever, sweating, fatigue, trembling or shaking of the hands, blue/purple nail beds.
Based on the information obtained during investigation, it was determined that parent was not informed of child's injury during pick up time.

During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence found to determine that a child's parent was not notified when a mosquito bite on the child's face that had occurred at home became swollen and required medical attention.
